page: Amazon Web Services c7g.large is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V1 model running at 2.6 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core and memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng benchmark scored 1532.38, and the Geekbench single-core score reached 1437.0, both falling into the average category. However, multi-core performance is limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2580.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 3043.08. Memory performance shows a read-only large block bandwidth of 52.81 GB/sec, but write bandwidth drops to 20.28 GB/sec. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware AES, though Passmark CPU encryption tests registered a lower score of 273.96.

Given its compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and ARM-based architecture, the c7g.large offers a cost-efficient entry point for ARM64 development, lightweight web serving, and basic text processing workloads. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or complex mathematical simulations due to its lower multi-core and memory benchmark ratings.
